items.title: Chipotle is opening 4 new Ontario locations — here's when and where
items.summary: New Ontario Chipotle locations will open in Mississauga, Kingston, Ottawa and Oshawa. Chipotle is currently on track to grow its Canadian restaurant footprint by approximately 30 per cent in 2026. Chipotle Mexican Grill is continuing to expand, with four new locations expected to open in Ontario before the end of 2026. The Ontario expansion includes locations in Mississauga, Kingston, Ottawa and Oshawa, with the Oshawa location marking the first in that city. Here’s where Chipotle will be opening in each city and the confirmed opening dates and target openings for each. A post shared by Chipotle Canada (@chipotlecanada) A Chipotle spokesperson released the official addresses, opening dates and targeted opening dates for the four new Ontario locations.

items.title: Mississauga City Hall and clock tower to light up yellow for antibullying campaign
items.summary: The illumination will mark #NoGoodWay Day, which aims to promote inclusive language for people with intellectual disabilities. The city will light up the clock tower and city hall in yellow on Nov. 18 Mississauga’s clock tower will be illuminated yellow on Nov. 18 to mark a national antibullying campaign. m. on Wednesday to mark the #NoGoodWay Day campaign. Led by motionball for Special Olympics, the event aims to promote inclusive language for individuals with intellectual disabilities and to end the casual and negative use of the R-word, the organization said in a press release. The 2026 campaign — from Nov. 4 to Nov. 18 — focused on raising awareness about the harmful impact of using the R-word and called on people to be superheroes in their communities by championing positive change. “Together, we as Canadians can use our voices to challenge stereotypes, spark conversations, and help create communities where everyone, especially those with intellectual disabilities, is treated with the respect, inclusion and the dignity they deserve,” said Paul Etherington, motionball’s co-founder, in the release. Participants are encouraged to wear yellow in support, sign an online pledge to promote inclusive language and share videos of themselves symbolically destroying the R-word by tearing, deleting or erasing it.

items.title: Mississauga’s data centre moratorium facing second challenge
items.summary: Mississauga’s one-year ban on data centre construction in the city is facing a second challenge at the Ontario Land Tribunal, Global News has learned, this time from a Toronto-based real estate investment firm. Montcrest Asset Management, which is proposing to build a data centre in the Eglinton Avenue East and Tahoe Boulevard area, is asking the tribunal to exempt their project from Mississauga’s moratorium. This comes as Prologis, an American supply chain warehouse developer, is also in the process of challenging the ban with the tribunal. Mississauga became one of the first cities in Canada to approve a one-year data centre moratorium, which went into effect in September. It was unanimously supported by city council, with one of its major backers being councillor-turned-mayor Alvin Tedjo. “There’s a lot of concerns about power consumption, the creation of heat islands and the noise attenuation that’s going to be happening,” Tedjo said prior to voting on the moratorium.

items.title: Prologis takes Mississauga to OLT over data centre moratorium
items.summary: An American logistics and warehouse developer is appealing the City of Mississauga’s one-year moratorium on data centre development, arguing the temporary ban lacks a sound planning rationale and has delayed a proposed project. San Francisco-based Prologis filed an appeal with the Ontario Land Tribunal in November, challenging the city’s interim control bylaw, which took effect in September following a unanimous council vote. The company applied in 2025 to build a two-storey, 220,000-square-foot data centre on former farmland near Tenth Line and Argentia Road in Mississauga. “After careful consideration of Council’s decision and the options available to us, Prologis has filed an appeal with the Ontario Land Tribunal regarding the City of Mississauga’s Interim Control By-law,” Global News reported. “Our commitment to Mississauga remains unchanged. ” Mississauga council imposed a one-year moratorium on new data centre development on Jul. 29, giving municipal staff a chance to prepare a report on potential impacts of facilities. Residents opposed to data centre development raised questions about the scale of operations, impact of water resources, electricity use and noise. Prologis submitted a proposal in August 2025, seeking a zoning by-law amendment and site plan approval for a two-storey, 220,000-sq. ft. data centre at Tenth Line West and Argentia Road.

items.title: Mississauga council sworn in — new mayor’s 1st directive is tax freeze
items.summary: Councillors say longer shelter stays are often needed to acc… A familiar face will continue to lead the region comprising … Mayor Alvin Tedjo pledges affordability, economic growth and innovation at city hall as Mississauga kicks off its 2026-2030 term. Mississauga’s city council, newly elected for the 2026-30 term, at the inaugural ceremony on Nov. 16. Mississauga’s newly elected city council was sworn into office on Nov. 16 at the Living Arts Centre, marking the start of the 2026-30 term. Along with Mayor Alvin Tedjo, nine incumbent councillors and two newcomers took their declarations of office before a nearly full main auditorium. Tedjo received prolonged applause and a standing ovation from the audience and council colleagues after receiving the mayor’s chain of office — the ceremonial regalia presented to a mayor upon taking office — and during his inaugural address. Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services’ pipe and drum band performed at the inaugural ceremony on Nov. 16.

items.title: Motorcyclist suffers life-threatening injuries in crash with minivan in Mississauga
items.summary: A motorcyclist suffered life-threatening injuries and another person was taken to hospital after a collision involving a motorcycle and a minivan in Mississauga. Peel Regional Police say the crash happened Tuesday afternoon (Nov. 17) on Dundas Street West near Fifth Line. m. after the motorcycle and minivan collided. An adult male riding the motorcycle was taken to hospital in serious condition. A second person was also transported to hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries, according to additional reporting by CityNews. The circumstances surrounding the collision have not been released, and police have not indicated what may have caused the crash. Westbound Dundas Street was closed between Fifth Line and the collision scene while officers investigated. Drivers were advised to use alternate routes. The closure caused traffic disruptions in the area during the afternoon commute. Peel Regional Police have not released the identities or ages of those involved.

items.title: Reporters Press Tedjo for Specifics on Tax Freeze Savings, Get Few Answers at First Scrum
items.summary: According to The Pointer, Mississauga Mayor Alvin Tedjo faced repeated questions from reporters on how he intends to pay for the two-year property tax freeze he promised during his campaign. The outlet reports Tedjo spoke to media following the Nov. 16 inauguration of the new city council, reiterating his commitment to affordability without naming which departments or expenditures he would cut. He told reporters efficiencies need to be found but offered few specifics on where those savings would come from, according to The Pointer. Tedjo said the city needs to tighten its own belt before asking residents to do the same, adding that the first budget will show the freeze can be delivered. The outlet notes the tax freeze was the central plank of Tedjo's mayoral campaign, and he said achieving it would require pursuing parallel strategies at City Hall.

Unprotected Floor Opening at Mississauga Wastewater Plant Led to $100,000 OHSA Fine
items.summary: According to the Ontario Ministry of Labour, the Ontario Clean Water Agency was fined $100,000 after pleading guilty to an Occupational Health and Safety Act offence tied to a workplace fall in Mississauga. The ministry says a worker was critically injured after falling through an unprotected floor opening at a wastewater treatment facility on Nov. 30, 2023. Workers were installing a new motor pump that day, and the job required opening floor hatches at several levels so a crane could lower the motor to a lower subfloor, the ministry said. An electrician and a helper opened the hatches and prepared the area, and a maintenance lead was then told about an issue and told workers to go to lunch, according to the ministry. The agency, which provides water treatment services across Ontario, pleaded guilty in Provincial Offences Court in Mississauga on Sept. 28, the ministry reported.
